title: How To Avoid A Stress-Filled End To The School Year ool-year/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: With summer visibly approaching, Linsin acknowledges that students grow chatty, restless, and prone to misbehavior in the final days of school, and offers three countermeasures. First, slow down deliberately — pausing longer between sentences and activities and refusing to move on until students are settled. Second, front-load academic rigor rather than saving fun activities for a final cram, since compelling lessons and independent projects keep students purposeful (and, he claims, happier). Third, stay fully consistent with the management plan rather than letting minor misbehavior slide, which he says is the biggest mistake teachers make as the year winds down and a common cause of relationships souring in the final week. He closes by reframing the end of the year around relationships and memories rather than sugar highs and freedom from responsibility.
points: The end-of-year antidote to restlessness is to deliberately slow down — longer pauses, calmer pace, refusing to move on until students are settled.
Front-load academic rigor and independent projects rather than saving all fun activities for a final cram at the very end.
The biggest end-of-year mistake is letting minor misbehavior slide, which causes tension even after a good year of rapport.
Reframe the final days around relationships and memories rather than sugar highs and freedom from responsibility.
quotes: They become chatty and restless. They become distracted and excitable.
The best antidote to the frenzy and commotion of the last few days of school is to slow down .

Not only does this keep your students purposeful and on-task, but because they’ve built up their independent work muscles over the preceding months, it provides an opportunity to make some of the biggest academic gains of the year.
The biggest mistake teachers make as they near the end is that they turn a blind eye to less severe misbehavior.
It isn’t unusual for teachers to experience good relationships throughout the year only to have them disintegrate during the final week.
By slowing down, focusing on academics, and holding tight to your promises , you can avoid the stress that affects so many teachers this time of year.
It’s about the smiles and tears. It’s about the hugs and thank yous.
